content.inline:
# Networks: Protonet, testnets, local

- **Protonet** is the live production network: peer `peer.convex.live:18888` (18888 is the standard peer port). Everything done there is real and permanent — coins, actors, names.
- **Testnets** exist for experimentation and tooling; their endpoints change and their state may be reset, so use the one the owner or the venue configuration names rather than a guess. A testnet may offer a faucet; on Protonet coins come from an existing holder.
- A **local network** (`convex local start` from a Convex build) is the right place to develop and test an actor before it touches Protonet.

## Talking to a network

The query and transact operations connect to the `peer` given in the call, falling back to the operation's configured default; with neither they fail with "No Convex endpoint provided" — so pass `peer` explicitly when in doubt, and say which network you used when you report. Queries are free and safe on any network; a transaction must go to the network the owner intends — confirm it before signing.

## Checking a network

Keep status queries small: `(balance #13)`, `*juice-price*` (the genesis price is 10, which Protonet runs), `(account #13)`. Never fetch `*state*` — it is the whole network.

Networks upgrade by scheduled migrations that raise the **protocol version** from 0 at genesis; a fresh network starts at the latest version, and Protonet moves when an upgrade activates. Some library behaviours differ between genesis and version 1 (trust checks failing closed, the token `:max-supply` default), so ask which version a network runs when a contract misbehaves.
